class_name: 順接-限定-ナイコトニハ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: States an obligation in everyday speech: the ないと clause names what has to happen, and the consequence is often dropped (そろそろ行かないと。), an ellipsis only the obligation reading allows. Its sibling ないことには is heavier and wants a main clause saying nothing can proceed; ないと is lighter and takes any main clause. なきゃ and なくちゃ are the casual contractions, なければ and なくては neutral, ねば classical and bookish.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]く出[で]ないと、終電[しゅうでん]に間[ま]に合[あ]わないよ。
examples.english: We've got to leave soon or we'll miss the last train.

examples.ruby: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]まないと、熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がらない。
examples.english: The fever won't come down unless you take the medicine.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]までに返事[へんじ]しないと、席[せき]がなくなる。
examples.english: I have to reply by tomorrow or I'll lose my spot.

patterns.usage_note: Presents the preceding clause as an indispensable prerequisite: until it happens, nothing else follows (現場を見ないことには、原因は分からない). The main clause is regularly negative or says matters cannot proceed (判断できない, 話にならない, 始まらない). Its sibling ないと is the ordinary conversational equivalent and carries no such restriction. ないことにゃ is the colloquial contraction, used in speech rather than writing.

examples.ruby: 現場[げんば]を見[み]ないことにゃ、原因[げんいん]なんて分[わ]かるもんか。
examples.english: Without laying eyes on the site, how's anyone supposed to work out the cause?

examples.ruby: 元手[もとで]を用意[ようい]しないことにゃ、商売[しょうばい]は始[はじ]まらん。
examples.english: Without putting up some seed money, there's no business to speak of.

examples.ruby: 直接[ちょくせつ]話[はな]してみないことにゃ、本当[ほんとう]のところは分[わ]からん。
examples.english: Without talking to him face to face, you'll never know the real story.
